from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Snell’s Law: The Geometric Rule", ["Snell's Law predicts how light bends.", "Wavefronts hit the medium at an angle.", "Slowing down causes the wavefront to pivot."])
        
        # Define objects
        boundary = Line(start=np.array([-2, 0, 0]), end=np.array([2, 0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(boundary, 'C3')
        
        normal = DashedLine(start=np.array([0, 1.5, 0]), end=np.array([0, -1.5, 0]), color="#808080")
        self.place_at_grid(normal, 'C3')
        
        incident_ray = Arrow(start=np.array([-1.5, 1.5, 0]), end=np.array([0, 0, 0]), color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        refracted_ray = Arrow(start=np.array([0, 0, 0]), end=np.array([1, -1.5, 0]), color="#FFCC00", buff=0)
        
        # Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(incident_ray), Create(boundary), Create(normal), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(refracted_ray), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFCC00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Visualization", [
            "Snell's Law is n1 sin theta1 equals n2 sin theta2.",
            "The beam bends toward or away from normal.",
            "Angles change in real-time as beam rotates."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Graph sin(theta 1) versus sin(theta 2).
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1, 0.2], y_range=[0, 1, 0.2], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "D4")
        self.add(axes)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the slope representing n1/n2.
        slope_label = MathTex("n_1/n_2", color="#FF5500").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "E4")
        self.play(Write(slope_label), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5500")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a coordinate plane tracking incident angles.
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[-1, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "B5")
        angle = ValueTracker(PI/4)
        beam = always_redraw(lambda: Line(ORIGIN, 1.5 * np.array([np.sin(angle.get_value()), np.cos(angle.get_value()), 0]), color="#808080"))
        self.add(beam)
        beam.move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(PI/6), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#808080")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "Refraction allows us to see clearly.",
            "Eyes focus light onto the retina.",
            "Refraction is fundamental to all lenses."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Straw in glass visualization
        glass = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=2.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2)
        water = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0)
        water.align_to(glass, DOWN)
        straw = Line(UP*1.2, DOWN*1.3, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=6)
        straw.rotate(0.2, about_point=ORIGIN)
        
        straw_group = VGroup(glass, water, straw)
        self.place_at_grid(straw_group, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(straw_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Eye diagram representation (Simplified)
        eye = Circle(radius=0.7, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        pupil = Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        light_ray = Arrow(LEFT*1.5, ORIGIN, color="#00FFFF", buff=0)
        
        eye_group = VGroup(eye, pupil, light_ray)
        self.place_at_grid(eye_group, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(eye_group))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Summary text
        summary = VGroup(
            Text("n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2)", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("Refraction is Everywhere!", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(summary, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(summary))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: Hook & The Prerequisite: Light's Speed in Vacuum
sections.content: Start with a 30-second visual hook showing a 'broken' straw in a glass of water. Briefly recap that light travels at a constant speed (c) in a vacuum, which serves as our baseline reference.
sections.example: An archerfish hunting: It must account for the shift in perceived position to hit its prey through the water-air interface.

sections.title: Defining Refractive Index (n)
sections.content: Introduce the refractive index as a measure of 'optical density.' Use a graphical representation: A runner (light) moving on a track (vacuum) vs. moving through deep sand (a dense medium). The formula n = c / v is displayed as a simple ratio.
sections.example: Comparing light passing through air (n≈1) vs. diamond (n≈2.42), showing the corresponding 'speed limit' reduction in the material.

sections.title: Snell’s Law: The Geometric Rule
sections.content: Visualize the bending process. Use a 2D animation of a wavefront (represented by parallel lines) hitting a boundary at an angle. As one side hits the medium first and slows down, the entire 'wavefront' pivots.
sections.example: A marching band turning a corner: When the soldiers on the inside slow down, the whole line automatically pivots toward the slower medium.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization
sections.content: Present Snell's Law (n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)). Instead of just text, use an interactive-style overlay showing the angles θ1 and θ2 changing in real-time as the light beam rotates toward or away from the 'normal' line.
sections.example: A laser pointer shining from air into a glass prism, showing the relationship between the incident angle and the refracted angle on a coordinate grid.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclude by connecting the theory to human vision and technology. Summarize that refraction is the basis for all lens-based devices.
sections.example: The human eye: How the cornea and lens refract incoming light to focus a sharp image onto the retina, much like a camera lens focusing light onto a sensor.
